#!/bin/sh
# Issue a fresh server certificate signed by the local node1 CA and reload
# nginx so it picks up the new cert/key without dropping connections.
set -e

commands.command: id nginx; sudo chown root:nginx /etc/nginx/certs; sudo chmod 750 /etc/nginx/certs; ls -la /etc/nginx/certs
commands.stdout: uid=997(nginx) gid=995(nginx) groups=995(nginx)
commands.stderr: ls: cannot open directory /etc/nginx/certs: Permission denied

commands.command:
sudo openssl genrsa -out /tmp/tmp.key 2048 >/dev/null 2>&1
sudo mkdir -p /etc/nginx/certs
NODE_IP_ADDR="$NODE_IP"
cat > /tmp/san.cnf <<EOF
[req]
distinguished_name = dn
req_extensions = v3_req
prompt = no
[dn]
CN = node1
[v3_req]
subjectAltName = @alt_names
[alt_names]
DNS.1 = node1
IP.1 = ${NODE_IP_ADDR}
EOF
sudo openssl req -new -key /tmp/tmp.key -out /tmp/tmp.csr -config /tmp/san.cnf
sudo openssl x509 -req -in /tmp/tmp.csr -CA /etc/nginx/ca/ca.crt -CAkey /etc/nginx/ca/ca.key -CAcreateserial -out /tmp/tmp.crt -days 1 -sha256 -extfile /tmp/san.cnf -extensions v3_req
sudo install -m 0644 /tmp/tmp.crt /etc/nginx/certs/cert.crt
sudo install -m 0640 -o root -g nginx /tmp/tmp.key /etc/nginx/certs/cert.key
sudo rm -f /tmp/tmp.key /tmp/tmp.csr /tmp/tmp.crt /tmp/san.cnf
sudo ls -la /etc/nginx/certs/
